title: The Painter Lady vs. Precision Paint Experts
description: New homeowner comparing The Painter Lady and Precision Paint Experts? A plain-language guide to hiring your first painter in North Central Florida.
h1: The Painter Lady vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: Just closed on a house and want it painted before the boxes are unpacked? Here is what first-time buyers should ask any painting contractor.

questions: Should I paint my new house before I move in?
What should I ask a painter when hiring for the first time?

sections.h2: Hiring a painter for the first time
body: New homeowners sometimes end up with The Painter Lady and Precision Paint Experts on the same shortlist. You will not find opinions about any other company on this page. This guide is written for new owners who have never hired a painter and are not sure what a good proposal looks like.

Buying a home tends to surface a list of small surprises: scuffed walls, patched holes, dated colors, maybe a popcorn ceiling. Fresh paint tends to top the to-do list, and the days between getting the keys and the moving truck showing up are the simplest time to get it done.

sections.h2: Five questions for every painter you call
body: Start by asking how a contractor protects the house: floors, fixtures, outlets, and any landscaping close to the walls. A new owner may not know which features are original or hard to replace, so the walkthrough is a good time to point out anything you want handled with extra care.
Comparing proposals takes no technical knowledge of coatings, only these answers, written down:
bullets: Are you licensed and insured in Florida, and do your workers carry workers' comp?
Which rooms and surfaces are included, and which are not?
Which brand and product will you use, and in how many coats?
When can you start, and how many days will it take?
What happens if something is not right at the end?

body: Here is how we answer them. We are a locally owned company with over 15 years of painting behind us, holding a Florida license, a bond, and full insurance, and every painter on your new house is our employee covered by workers' comp; no subcontractors.

After a crew lead tours and measures your new place, you get an itemized proposal, typically one business day later, showing the rooms and surfaces in and out of scope, the prep, the primer and finish products, the number of coats, and the dates. No prices are published anywhere, since every house differs in square footage, condition, chosen product line, reach, and color count. Painting usually begins one to three weeks after you sign, so reach out as soon as your closing is on the calendar.

sections.h2: Projects worth doing before the furniture arrives
body: An empty house makes some jobs much simpler. With bare floors underneath, ceiling painting and popcorn removal goes far more smoothly; before scraping any texture, read our note on asbestos testing for popcorn ceilings. Wall patching through drywall repair and a full interior repaint can follow in the same visit. Painting every room in a newly purchased house generally takes from three days up to two weeks.
Already unpacked? No problem. The painters will slide and cover your things and finish one room before starting another, so there is no need to stay elsewhere.

If you are thinking about the outside too, it can wait. Outside work goes best in the drier October-to-May months while indoor rooms can be painted whenever you like, so plenty of first-time buyers do the interior right away and pencil in exterior painting for the next fall.

We can usually come see your new home within 48 hours. When the work is finished, you inspect it with the crew lead and anything you flag is made right before we call it complete; the labelled leftover paint stays in the house for you. Ask for a free estimate, then hold it up against every other proposal you gather.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to paint a house I just bought?
faqs.a: There is no price list, because the figure depends on your home's measured area, the state of its surfaces, the product line, access, and how many colors you pick. A free itemized quote gives you the real number.

faqs.q: Is it better to paint before or after moving in?
faqs.a: Before is easier, particularly for ceilings, though after works fine too: the crew handles the furniture and moves through the house one space at a time.

faqs.q: Do I have to move out while the interior is painted?
faqs.a: No. You can live there throughout; painters take care of shifting and covering furniture and work around your household room by room.
